description: Creates a new Sentry release for an existing organization, associating it with specified projects that must belong to that organization.

inputSchema.description: Request to create a new release for an organization.

commits.description: An optional list of commit data to be associated with the release. Commits must include the `id` parameter (the SHA of the commit). Optionally, include `repository`, `message`, `patch_set`, `author_name`, `author_email`, and `timestamp` for richer integration and better suspect commit tracking.

items.description: Commit details to associate with a release.

author_email.description: The email of the commit author. Providing the author's email is required to enable the suggested assignee feature in Sentry.
author_email.title: Author Email

author_name.description: The name of the commit author.
author_name.title: Author Name

id.description: The unique identifier of the commit, typically the full commit SHA.
id.title: Id

patch_set.description: A list of files changed in the commit. Specifying the patch_set is necessary to power Sentry features like suspect commits and suggested assignees.

items.description: Details of a file change within a commit.

path.description: The path to the file that was changed. Both forward and backward slashes are supported.
path.title: Path

type.description: The type of change that happened in the file for this commit. 'A' for added, 'M' for modified, 'D' for deleted.
type.title: Type

items.title: PatchSetRequest

patch_set.title: Patch Set

repository.description: The full name of the repository the commit belongs to. If this field is not given, Sentry will generate a name in the format "organization-<organization_id>" (e.g., if the organization ID is 123, the repository name will be "organization-123").
repository.title: Repository

timestamp.description: The commit timestamp in ISO 8601 format. This is used to sort the commits. If a timestamp is not included, the commits will remain sorted in the order they are provided.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

items.title: CommitsRequest

commits.title: Commits

dateReleased.description: An optional ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the release went live. If not provided, the current time is assumed by Sentry.
dateReleased.title: Date Released

organization_id_or_slug.description: The ID or slug of the Sentry organization.
organization_id_or_slug.title: Organization Id Or Slug

projects.description: A list of project slugs that are part of this release. These projects must belong to the specified organization.
projects.title: Projects

ref.description: An optional commit reference, such as a branch name or a tag. This is useful if a tagged version has been provided (e.g., `version` is 'v1.0.0' and `ref` is 'refs/tags/v1.0.0').
ref.title: Ref

refs.description: An optional way to indicate the start and end commits for each repository included in a release. Head commits must include `repository` and `commit` (the HEAD SHA). They can optionally include `previousCommit` (the SHA of the HEAD of the previous release), which should be specified if this is the first time you've sent commit data. `commit` may also contain a range in the form of `previousCommit..commit`.

items.description: Commit range for a repository within a release.

commit.description: The commit SHA for the current release's HEAD. Can also be a range like `previousCommit..commit`.
commit.title: Commit

previousCommit.description: The commit SHA for the previous release's HEAD. Recommended if this is the first time sending commit data.
previousCommit.title: Previous Commit

repository.description: The full name of the repository the commit belongs to.
repository.title: Repository

items.title: RefsRequest

refs.title: Refs

url.description: An optional URL that points to the release. This can be a link to a GitHub release, a CI build page, or an internal changelog.
url.title: Url

version.description: A unique identifier for this release. Can be a semantic version number, a commit hash, or any other string that uniquely identifies this release.
version.title: Version
